Command-Line Reference > sa sla sab (build / workspace / disasm)

sa sla sab (build / workspace / disasm)

sa sla sab is the explicit entry point for SAB bytecode (opt-in), with three subcommands: build, workspace, and disasm; sa slab ... is its short alias. SAB was sealed on 2026-11-15 (tag sab-sealed-2026-11-15), and its positioning is an optimization direction rather than the production path — default builds and tests always take SA text, and the commands on this page produce SAB only when explicitly invoked by name. After reading this page you can produce SAB artifacts on their own for inspection, and disassemble existing SAB files.

Syntax

usage: sa sla sab <build|workspace|disasm> [options]
       sa slab <build|workspace|disasm> [options]

usage: sa sla sab build [file] [-p <package>] [--out <file.sab>]
usage: sa sla sab workspace [-p <package>] [--sab-out <file.sab>] [sa-build-exe-options...]
usage: sa sla sab disasm <file.sab> [--out <file.sa>]

sab build

NameDescription
fileThe input .sla file; when omitted, the member entry point is resolved via the workspace.
-o, --out <file.sab>Additionally write out a user-visible SAB file. When omitted, only the managed cache artifact is updated.
-p, --packageSelect the workspace member package.
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla sab build tests/test_sab_direct.sla
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla sab build tests/test_sab_direct.sla --out /tmp/test_sab_direct.sab
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa slab build tests/test_sab_direct.sla --out /tmp/test_sab_direct.sab

A successful output looks like Sla Compiler: Successfully compiled ... to SAB /tmp/test_sab_direct.sab (managed cache .sla-cache/sab/....sab).; when --out is not given it is ... to managed SAB .sla-cache/sab/....sab.

NoteThe file path of sab build does not parse @test test bodies: after a source file containing @test is compiled via sab build, the function body of each test_decl is empty. Therefore a PASS obtained by handing that artifact to sa test is an empty-run result and does not constitute test evidence; the only SAB path that truly parses and executes test bodies is when sa sla test explicitly selects the SAB backend (--test-backend sab; the default auto now lands on the SA text path). Ordinary (non-@test) function bodies are compiled in full on every path.

sab workspace

Resolves the members of the current sa.mod workspace, takes the managed SAB compilation, then delegates to sa build-exe to generate an executable. It does not accept a source file argument.

NameDescription
-p, --packageSelect the member package.
--sab-out <file.sab>Additionally write out a SAB artifact for inspection.
--emit-sabWrite a sibling .sab next to the source file.
Remaining argumentsPassed through to sa build-exe (--sab-out/--emit-sab themselves are stripped); --jobs auto is added automatically by default.
# 在 workspace 根目录执行
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla sab workspace --sab-out /tmp/workspace.sab -o /tmp/workspace_app
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa slab workspace -p my_app -o /tmp/my_app

sab disasm

Disassembles a SAB file into text for debugging; not part of the compilation path. The maximum input is 16 MiB.

NameDescription
file.sabRequired. The SAB file to disassemble.
-o, --out <file.sa>Write the text SA debug output to a file; when omitted, print to stdout.
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla sab disasm .sla-cache/sab/main-1a2b3c4d.sab --out /tmp/main.disasm.sa
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa slab disasm /tmp/test_sab_direct.sab | less

Output locations

  • Managed SAB: always written to .sla-cache/sab/<stem>-<hash>.sab, and not rewritten when the content is unchanged.
  • User-visible SAB: written only when explicitly requested — sab build uses --out, sab workspace uses --sab-out or --emit-sab.
  • Executable: sab workspace delegates to sa build-exe, which writes it according to -o.
